$comment: Example outputs of `doan design-skill [id] --json`, shared by the Go and TypeScript tests. Every other file in this directory is a complete cli-envelope v1 and validates against schema/cli-envelope.v1.schema.json.

The CLI used for these examples reports version "dev". result.version is the producing doan version; consumers show it as provenance and must not reject a result because it differs from their own version.

list.json lists only the presets that exist in the catalog at the time; tests must not assume a fixed count. It carries id, title, description and scope per preset, in catalog order, and never a body or sources.

A single preset result carries version, preset (the same four fields as a list row), body and sources. The body is complete only when it ends with the line `[doan:design-skill] end of preset <id> v<version>` followed by a newline, where <id> is preset.id and <version> is result.version. This marker differs from the `doan skill` guide's `[doan:skill] end of guide v<version>`.

Every rejected id below fails with code usage_error and exit 2 (`doan design-skill --json -- <id>`; after `--` every argument is the id, so `--json` must come first). code, v and ok are the contract. message and nextSteps are illustrative: the message names the rejected id, so it differs per input.

Upstream names that Doan does not publish (craft, live, overdrive, optimize, init) are rejected like any unknown id; there is no alias. `init` here is the upstream command name, not the CLI command `doan init`.
